input.quote: (b) Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement. Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
input.rationale: The only audit right binding us is Article V.IV(b) (p0073), with cost allocation in p0064. It uses an independent CPA/audit professional and puts cost on Licensor unless a discrepancy exceeds 5%, which already matches the preferred cost and auditor elements. However, it contains no frequency limit (audits could be demanded repeatedly), no prior-notice requirement (the 30-day window is a deadline for us to permit the audit, not notice to us), and no business-hours, confidentiality, off-site or system-access protections. Unlimited audits on no notice is walk-away territory and fails the fallback (once per year on 15 days' notice), so we have added the missing guardrails at the preferred level with two short edits, leaving the auditor-selection and 5% cost-shift terms untouched.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality, off-site and no-system-access limits to the Licensor audit right
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added the standard audit guardrails to Article V.IV(b): one audit per 12-month period on 30 days' prior written notice, during business hours, off-site where possible, by a confidentiality-bound auditor, with no direct access to our systems. The existing independent-auditor and 5% cost-shifting terms are unchanged.

ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
ops.newText: Licensor may conduct such an audit no more than once in any 12-month period, upon at least 30 days' prior written notice to Licensee.

ops.text: Audits shall be conducted during Licensee's normal business hours and off-site where possible; the auditor shall be bound by written confidentiality obligations; and neither Licensor nor the auditor shall have direct access to Licensee's systems.
